evidence: Wikipedia's article on the Yardbirds: the band became the house band at the Crawdaddy Club in Richmond, succeeding the Rolling Stones, under manager Giorgio Gomelsky, who also set up their tours backing Sonny Boy Williamson in 1963 and 1964.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Both bands came out of the same Richmond club playing the same Chicago blues. 'Come On' is the Stones' first single, a Chuck Berry song. 'For Your Love', two years later, is the Yardbirds going the other way: harpsichord, bongos, a pop chorus. Listen for how one scene's house band could turn into two very different careers, and why Clapton left over this record.

explanation.age13: The Yardbirds became the house band at the Crawdaddy Club in Richmond, west London, after the Rolling Stones left. They played blues there and backed an American blues singer on tour before turning to pop.
explanation.adult: A scene edge through a room, the Crawdaddy, and a manager, Giorgio Gomelsky, who ran both the club nights and the band. It is where the Stones, the Yardbirds and through them Clapton, Beck and Page all started.
